newsitem.title: CANADA: Falconbridge to reply to union offer Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Falconbridge to reply to union offer Wednesday.

text.p: Falconbridge Ltd said on Tuesday it would respond on Wednesday to the latest proposal on shift scheduling from the union representing Falconbridge's striking Ontario workers.
"The company is looking over the document and will respond (Wednesday)," Falconbridge spokesman Brian McLeod said in a telephone interview on Tuesday.
McLeod declined to comment on the union's offer.

Full scale contract talks broke off on August 1 when about 1,400 unionized workers walked off the job at Falconbridge's Sudbury, Ontario operations. But sub-committees have recently begun work on the key issue of shift scheduling.
"The delivery of the counter proposals went well and now we're waiting for the company to respond," said Rolly Gauthier, local 598 president of the Canadian Auto Workers union.
Falconbridge's Sudbury operations last year produced 45,700 metric tons of nickel, 50,000 metric tons of copper and 1,600 metric tons of cobalt, including custom feed.
